text:
Jamie (support): FYI customer Oakwell Health is seeing a sudden latency + 401s and a billing spike. They say requests supposed to hit eu-west but logs show ap-south. Can we triage?
Priya (support): Can you paste the request/response traces and any trace_id?
Jamie (support): Trace IDs and sample request below. Notice header `X-Preferred-Region: eu-west` but routed to ap-south and token failed.
```
Request: POST /v1/generate
Headers: {
  "Authorization": "Bearer tok_eyJ...",
  "X-Preferred-Region": "eu-west",
  "User-Agent": "oakwell/1.2"
}
Response: 401 Unauthorized
Logs: route.decided=ap-south, route.reason=auto_divert_capacity, queue_depth=128, trace_id=tr-0a1b2c3d
```
Kai (eng-sre): capacity_fallback kicked in when eu-west queue > 100. That matches the queue_depth. But auto_divert policy should prefer dedicated failover list, not arbitrary next region.
Morgan (infra-routing): I rolled a small change yesterday to routing evaluation that made `pinned_region` a soft hint under high-load — commit 3f1b7c. Looks like weight ordering got inverted in some cases. Will check. :eyes:
Alex (billing): If traffic was diverted cross-region we need to flag potential egress charges for the customer. If confirmed, propose issuing a credit; please capture estimated token counts. :moneybag:
Priya (support): Customer reports token volume ~120k tokens in 10m window while diversion lasted ~6m. Will attach raw usage.
Jamie (support): Repro steps I'm running locally to trigger:
```
# simulate short-burst that fills eu-west queue
for i in {1..250}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN" -H "X-Preferred-Region: eu-west" -d '{"prompt":"x"}' &
done
```
I can reproduce diversion to ap-south after ~100 concurrent in-flight.
Kai (eng-sre): Can you capture the full route decision payload (routing.debug=true) and post. Also, is the token scope region-locked? That'd explain 401 when diverted.
Jamie (support): Added routing.debug output: `{"pinned_region":"eu-west","available_capacity":{"eu-west":0,"ap-south":12},"policy":"capacity_fallback_v2","selected":"ap-south"}`. Token scope is `scope:region:eu-west` so 401 expected when hitting ap-south.
Morgan (infra-routing): Found the bug: when capacity_fallback_v2 calculates fallback order it accidentally sorts by region name instead of remaining_capacity after the 3f1b7c change. So ap-south got picked because "ap-south" sorts before others. Reverting the sort in routing evaluator should fix. I'm putting a hotfix PR.
deploy-bot: deploy queued for routing/hotfix-3f1b7c-revert (staging) — build 4532.
Kai (eng-sre): After hotfix we should also add a guard: if selected_region != pinned_region and token is region-scoped then abort and return 409 with message suggesting retry with cross-region token or pin. That avoids silent 401s.
Alex (billing): Hold on credits until we confirm duration. But earmarking provisional credit for Oakwell ~6m * estimated egress USD 0.08/min = ~$0.5k. Will finalize after postmortem.
Priya (support): Notifying customer that we're investigating, asking for any additional logs and confirming we've opened escalation.
Jamie (support): Assigned to infra-routing (Morgan) and eng-sre (Kai). Priority: P0 for customer impact + billing. Will update when hotfix is live.
Morgan (infra-routing): Hotfix deployed to staging, running load test. If green will push to prod in 15m.
Kai (eng-sre): I'll add a short page to runbook: "How to detect capacity-divert with region-scoped tokens" and mitigation steps.
Jamie (support): Customer updated: they saw normal traffic resume ~14:32 UTC. I'll follow up on credits once you confirm. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
